key_facts: On Oct. 13, 2023 Best Buy confirmed Plaintiff's application for General Warehouse Worker / 2nd Shift at $22.60, requisition 928556BR, Tracy warehouse 6653 Hopkins Road. On Oct. 17 at 3:47 p.m. GM Jose Tapia sent a congratulations offer requiring Candidate Zone acceptance, background-check information, and authorization. Plaintiff accepted. At 4:22 p.m. Best Buy sent a background-authorization confirmation identifying First Advantage Consumer Center. At 4:30 p.m. First Advantage generated a Best Buy drug-test order, Q09078711, account BEST BUY 11759586. Plaintiff completed the screening. Best Buy then stopped the hire without communicating an independent post-screen reason. Federal draft alleges as ultimate facts on I&B that First Advantage furnished Plaintiff's § 290.46 information and Best Buy used it for the employment decision. Same-consumer First Advantage comparators from UPS/FedEx provide additional plausibility support.
procedural_status: Pre-filing federal redraft on branch matter39-edca-federal-redraft. Prior executed San Joaquin packet dated Sep. 8, 2026 was never filed and is historical only. Proposed federal forum: E.D. Cal., Sacramento. Draft uses dual jurisdiction: FCRA federal question if timely and independent diversity jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1332 based on Plaintiff's California citizenship, Best Buy Co., Inc.'s Minnesota citizenship, and a good-faith amount in controversy over $75,000. Arbitration policy referenced by the 2023 application must be obtained/audited before filing.
damages: Offer rate is $22.60/hour; weekly hours and start date are not fixed in the current record. Federal draft seeks nonduplicative actual economic damages from the lost accepted employment, timely remedies under Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A), and, only if timely, FCRA/ICRAA statutory and punitive remedies. Diversity amount-in-controversy is alleged in good faith to exceed $75,000, but final filing should ensure that allegation remains supportable without relying solely on a potentially time-barred civil penalty.
risk: Primary risks: (1) FCRA § 1681p actual/constructive discovery — Plaintiff knew in Oct. 2023 that Best Buy required a background check and First Advantage participated, so Count One needs a truthful later discovery event; (2) ICRAA § 1786.52 two-year discovery period; (3) § 290.46 limitations characterization — file before Oct. 2026 three-year anniversary and make compensatory statutory liability, not the civil penalty, load-bearing; (4) Best Buy arbitration policy; (5) exact employing/report-user entity. Merits pleading is strong on vendor identity because First Advantage is tied to Plaintiff's own Best Buy transaction.
